title: Iteration Patterns and Trace Tables
learningObjectives: Explain iteration patterns and trace tables and their execution flow.
Trace condition checks and state changes across iterations.
Select a suitable loop structure for a given problem.
Identify common termination and boundary mistakes.
Apply the loop pattern in an original small program.

understand.concept: Common iteration patterns include counting, accumulation, searching, filtering and nested traversal. Trace tables record state, condition, action and update for each pass.
understand.whyItMatters: Pattern recognition helps choose a loop and test it systematically.
understand.explain: Test empty, boundary and typical cases; trace state changes and verify termination.

examples.title: Search early exit
examples.explanation: Search stops at first match and records success.

examples.title: Trace while loop
examples.explanation: State trace: 1→2→4→8; stops after x becomes 8.

practise.guidedTask: Trace and annotate each of the five Iteration Patterns and Trace Tables examples. For every iteration, record the relevant variable values, condition result and action. Change one input or bound and predict the new behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ program demonstrating iteration patterns and trace tables in a practical scenario. Include at least three typical tests, two boundary tests, and one invalid or termination test. Explain how the loop terminates.
hints: Trace variables in a small table.
Prefer the simplest loop form for the task.
